Signing and verifying a message, whole or in pieces, with the post-quantum and hybrid algorithms, and the DSSE envelope that carries a signed statement.

Each section is one help page: what its functions are for, and the example
of the page as it runs. `?name` gives the arguments and the value in full.

## Sign and verify

`nqsign()`, `nqverify()`: `nqsign()` signs a message with ML-DSA (FIPS 204), SLH-DSA (FIPS 205), Ed25519 (RFC 8032) or a hybrid ML-DSA+Ed25519, whose signature verifies only when both parts do; `nqverify()` checks such a signature.

```{r nqsign}
k <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-44")
s <- nqsign(k$sk, "hello", "ML-DSA-44")
nqverify(k$pk, "hello", s, "ML-DSA-44")
nqverify(k$pk, "hellO", s, "ML-DSA-44")
# a context binds the signature to one purpose
s2 <- nqsign(k$sk, "hello", "ML-DSA-44", ctx = "invoices")
nqverify(k$pk, "hello", s2, "ML-DSA-44", ctx = "invoices")
nqverify(k$pk, "hello", s2, "ML-DSA-44")
# deterministic signatures repeat; hedged ones do not
identical(
  nqsign(k$sk, "hello", "ML-DSA-44", det = TRUE),
  nqsign(k$sk, "hello", "ML-DSA-44", det = TRUE)
)
# pre-hash: HashML-DSA with SHA-512
s3 <- nqsign(k$sk, "hello", "ML-DSA-44", ph = "sha512")
nqverify(k$pk, "hello", s3, "ML-DSA-44", ph = "sha512")
# a hybrid needs both halves to verify
h <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-44+Ed25519")
nqverify(h$pk, "hello", nqsign(h$sk, "hello", h$alg), h$alg)
# SLH-DSA, hash-based
sl <- nqkeygen("SLH-DSA-SHAKE-128f")
length(nqsign(sl$sk, "hello", sl$alg))
```

## Sign and verify a message given in pieces

`nqsigner()`, `nqverifier()`, `nqupdate()`, `nqfinish()`, `nqsignfile()`, `nqverifyfile()`: `nqsigner()` and `nqverifier()` start a signature or its check over a message that arrives in pieces; `nqupdate()` adds each piece, and `nqfinish()` gives the signature (the bytes `nqsign()` gives for the whole message with the same randomness) or whether it verifies. Only the piece at hand is held in memory. `nqsignfile()` and `nqverifyfile()` do it for a file, 64 KiB at a time.

```{r nqsigner}
k <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-44")
s <- nqsigner(k$sk, "ML-DSA-44")
nqupdate(s, "part one, ")
nqupdate(s, "part two")
sig <- nqfinish(s, det = TRUE)
identical(sig, nqsign(k$sk, "part one, part two", "ML-DSA-44", det = TRUE))
v <- nqverifier(k$pk, "ML-DSA-44")
nqupdate(v, "part one, part two")
nqfinish(v, sig = sig)
f <- tempfile()
writeBin(as.raw(0:255), f)
nqverifyfile(f, k$pk, nqsignfile(f, k$sk, "ML-DSA-44"), "ML-DSA-44")
unlink(f)
```

## ML-DSA with an external mu

`nqmu()`, `nqsignmu()`, `nqverifymu()`: `nqmu()` computes the 64-byte message representative mu of FIPS 204 for a message under a public key, as `nqsign()` computes it, so that a large message can be hashed apart from where the secret key is (a token, a hardware module). `nqsignmu()` signs that mu: the signature is the one `nqsign()` gives for the message with the same randomness. `nqverifymu()` checks a signature against a mu.

```{r nqmu}
k <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-44")
mu <- nqmu(k$pk, "a long message", "ML-DSA-44")
s <- nqsignmu(k$sk, mu, "ML-DSA-44", det = TRUE)
identical(s, nqsign(k$sk, "a long message", "ML-DSA-44", det = TRUE))
nqverifymu(k$pk, mu, s, "ML-DSA-44")
```

## DSSE envelopes

`nqdsse()`, `nqdsseverify()`: `nqdsse()` wraps a payload in a DSSE envelope (Dead Simple Signing Envelope, the signing wrapper of in-toto and SLSA), signed with any signature algorithm of `nqalgs()`; `nqdsseverify()` checks one.

```{r nqdsse}
k <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-65")
e <- nqdsse(k$sk, k$pk, '{"a":1}', "application/json", "ML-DSA-65")
cat(rawToChar(e))
v <- nqdsseverify(k$pk, e, "ML-DSA-65")
v$type
rawToChar(v$payload)
# another key does not verify it
other <- nqkeygen("ML-DSA-65")
is.null(nqdsseverify(other$pk, e, "ML-DSA-65"))
```
